title: DOE Genesis Mission award
body:
Honored and excited to announce that our team has been selected for a U.S. Department of Energy Genesis Mission Phase I Award.

While Texas A&M University is celebrating joining this historic national initiative, our project focuses on developing AI-powered digital twins to run complex nuclear physics experiments and maximize national beamtime productivity. Out of nearly 300 projects selected nationwide, we are thrilled to represent Texas A&M in pushing the boundaries of AI-driven scientific discovery.

Huge thanks to our co-investigators Ronald Garcia Ruiz (MIT), Abhishek Roy (TAMU), Ahmed Attia (ANL), Bernhard Maaß (ANL), Dan Melconian (TAMU), Kei Minamisono (FRIB) and Sven Leyffer (ANL), and to the Department of Energy for supporting this vision.

title: Anna, Henry and Meg join us as 2026 summer students
body:
Welcome y'all! They will work on projects ranging from commissioning a novel laser ablation ion source to developing an agentic control system and an AI-powered emulator for our ion optics simulations.

We acknowledge the support of the DOE TREND, TAMU Physics Department Summer Research and NSF REU programs.

title: LECM25 and the Precision Measurements workshop
body: Our group organised a satellite Workshop on Precision Measurements with Radioisotopes at LECM25, hosted at Texas A&M this year. The workshop brought together theorists and experimentalists from across the U.S. and was a big success — a second edition is planned for LECM26 at Argonne National Laboratory.

title: Groundbreaking of the Karthein Lab at Texas A&M
body: We are happy to announce the groundbreaking of the Karthein Lab at the Physics Department and the Cyclotron Institute of Texas A&M University. We have exciting projects in the pipeline and are actively looking for talented, motivated students and postdocs to join our efforts on campus, at MIT, and at the accelerator facilities FRIB in Michigan and CERN in Switzerland. Please reach out to lab@karthein.com.

title: Closing in on ¹⁰⁰Sn at CERN, in Nature Physics
body:
Our group published results from measurements at the precision laser spectrometer CRIS at CERN's radioactive ion beam facility ISOLDE in Nature Physics (journal, arXiv). The results present significant evidence for the doubly magic character of the ¹⁰⁰Sn nucleus, through measurements of the electromagnetic properties of several indium isotopes.

See also the feature article at Phys.org and the Department of Energy science highlight.

title: NEPTUNE theory paper in Physical Review Letters
body: Our group published a theory paper on one of our main projects, NEPTUNE, in Physical Review Letters (journal, arXiv). We present a technique using single molecular ions in a Penning trap that should amplify so-far unstudied symmetry-violating electroweak effects by more than twelve orders of magnitude compared with measurements in atoms, and we work through the method's statistical and systematic uncertainties in detail.
